ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of all UBOs, directors and officers against OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List; United Nations Security Council Consolidated List; Canadian sanctions regulations under the Special Economic Measures Act, S.C. 1992, c. 17; United Nations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. U-7; Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, S.C. 2017, c. 20 (Sergei Magnitsky Act); and applicable EU and UK financial sanctions lists. Enhanced Due Diligence applies for foreign PEPs, high-risk source jurisdictions, inconsistent source-of-funds explanations, or reliance on nominee shareholders. For ISIC 5911 commercial 3D animation and VFX production the standard client risk tier is Low_Risk_Standard, with no statutory industry license trigger.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry - Service Alberta, filed through authorized Alberta Registry Agents using the Corporate Registry System and NUANS Name Search portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Alberta corporate names may be in English, French, or a bilingual combination. Names using a non-official script must be transliterated or translated into English or French for NUANS search comparability and registry indexing. The corporate designator must appear in Latin characters, e.g., Inc., Corp., Ltd., Limited; a separate ordinary trade name for animation and VFX services may be used if distinguishable.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation or NUANS name search report is valid for 90 days and cannot be administratively extended; if incorporation is not completed within the window, a fresh NUANS search is required. If the proposed name is rejected, the filer may submit a written Request for Reconsideration to the Alberta Registrar of Corporations within 30 days of rejection, attaching the original rejection notice, a new NUANS report, written legal submissions on distinguishability, and proposed alternative names. If the Registrar affirms the refusal, judicial review may be sought by originating application to the Court of King's Bench of Alberta under the Alberta Rules of Court, with notice to the Registrar, normally within six months of the adverse decision.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual reception or remote-production address is acceptable for day-to-day operations of an ISIC 5911 animation studio, but the Alberta registered office must be a real civic street address in Alberta where process may be served and corporate records can be inspected. A pure mailbox or online virtual address without a physical Alberta location is not permissible as a statutory registered office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Baseline unannounced physical inspection risk is below 5% per year for a low-risk standard commercial animation/VFX corporation; risk rises to approximately 15-25% if the company relies on a mail-forwarding-only registered office, if any UBO is foreign-sourced with incomplete notarized documentation, or if corporate filings contain inconsistencies. For a fully compliant Alberta-registered business with a physical studio address in Calgary or Edmonton, annual unannounced inspection probability remains low.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9, as amended; ss. 6-13 (incorporation), s. 101 (registered office), s. 106 (records office), s. 108 (directors)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction (CORES electronic lodgement portal)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form 1) filed under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta); accompanied by Notice of Registered Office (Form 2) and Notice of Directors (Form 3)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; any class of shares may be issued for such consideration as the directors determine; no escrow account or capital deposit requirement under Alberta law
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLVED, that the Articles of Incorporation of the Corporation, as filed with the Alberta Corporate Registry, are hereby ratified and approved in full.

RESOLVED, that the allotment and issuance of Class A Common Shares to the subscribers named in the Subscription Agreement is approved, such shares to be issued fully paid and non-assessable upon receipt of the agreed subscription consideration.

RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Corporation is fixed at the address in Alberta stated in the Notice of Registered Office, and the records office is established at the registered office location.

RESOLVED, that the officers nominated by the Board are appointed, with authority to open banking accounts, execute commercial contracts, and implement all corporate filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry via accredited CORES service provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Request a NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) preliminary search through the Alberta Corporate Registry system; verify name distinctiveness against existing trademarks and corporate names; file a Name Reservation Request, which is valid for 90 days, naming the proposed legal name of the Corporation.
required_dossiers: Declaration of name usage and trademark due diligence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or protested, submit an alternate name of the same corporate family or apply for consent from the objecting entity; re-file a fresh name search within the 90-day reservation window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Execute Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Articles of Incorporation specifying the corporate name, registered office address in Alberta, share structure (including Class A Common Shares), number of directors (at least one) and any director residency restrictions; each incorporator signs the articles; obtain consent of each named director to act as director.
required_dossiers: Consent of each director to act
Registered office address confirmation in Alberta
Shareholder and director name, address and identification details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Registry query is cured by correcting technical deficiencies, filing a statement of amendment, and resubmitting the electronic package; any filing deficiency notice from the Registrar is resolved prior to the Certificate of Incorporation being issued.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Submission and Issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (CORES electronic lodgement service)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Articles of Incorporation and accompanying consents electronically via an accredited CORES service provider or the corporate registry internet application; pay the statutory filing fee; the system issues a filestampted Certificate of Incorporation with a unique Alberta Corporation Number upon approval.
required_dossiers: Proof of payment of the state filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, the registrant corrects the flagged fields and resubmits; if incorporation is rejected due to name issues, a new name reservation is obtained and the articles are refiled without duplication of fees where applicable.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Resolution, By-law Adoption and Share Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Corporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold an organizational meeting of directors or adopt a written board resolution; approve the form of share subscription agreements; allot and issue Class A Common Shares to the subscribers; adopt general operating by-laws; approve banking resolutions; authorize opening of corporate bank accounts and engagement of external counsel/accountants.
required_dossiers: Written board resolution or meeting minutes
Share subscription agreements and director resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a director is unavailable for the meeting, the resolution is passed by unanimous written consent signed by all directors in accordance with the Business Corporations Act (Alberta); all share certificates must be issued within the by-law prescribed period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Initial Corporate Registry Notices
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Notice of Registered Office (Form 2) and Notice of Directors (Form 3) within the statutory period following incorporation; maintain a registered office and records office at a physical address in Alberta, and ensure director information is current; pay any applicable administrative charge for late filings.
required_dossiers: Director residential or alternative address information
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notices are rejected for incomplete director addresses or office address issues, correct the filings through the CORES portal and resubmit within the cure period; failure to cure may result in administrative dissolution, which is remedied by restoration filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business Licence, Provincial Accounts and Regulatory Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal licensing department (e.g., City of Calgary or City of Edmonton) and Government of Alberta provincial agencies
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a municipal business licence for the treatment of the studio as a physical place of business; register with the Alberta Corporate Tax and Capital Tax (if applicable), the Workers' Compensation Board (WCB) for any employees, and the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) for corporate income tax and GST/HST accounts; confirm zoning compliance for a commercial office/animation studio.
required_dossiers: Commercial lease or office ownership documentation
CRA and Alberta tax registration forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If zoning or building compliance is flagged by the municipality, obtain a zoning development permit or variance and a building occupancy inspection report; for tax number delays, escalate through the CRA Business Window and Alberta Program Services.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Municipal Business Licensing Department (City of Calgary or City of Edmonton, as applicable) in coordination with Alberta Corporate Registry and Alberta Occupational Health and Safety (OHS)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Non-Residential Business Licence for Commercial Animation and VFX Studio (general business/office use)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Alberta Environment and Protected Areas (formerly Alberta Environment and Parks)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B (Registration) — solvent-based animation production is a computer-based studio operation with negligible discharge; a Full Environmental Impact Assessment is not triggered under the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act for office-based CGI production
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater discharge or additional VOC emissions generated by 3D animation work; compliance with municipal sanitary sewer use by-laws and Alberta Ambient Air Quality Objectives; electronic waste (computers, servers, monitors) must be disposed of through registered recycling streams under the Alberta Recycling Regulation; equipment cooling and HVAC must comply with the Canadian Environmental Protection Act, 1999 regarding refrigerants and ozone-depleting substances

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certification under the Alberta Fire Code (Fire Prevention Act) covering evacuation plan, fire extinguishers, alarm system and maximum occupancy; structural load inspection and building occupancy permit issued by the municipality for the leased commercial floor; Alberta Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) workplace clearance confirming ergonomic workstations, emergency lighting, electrical safety, and a first-aid kit as required for a small commercial office environment.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC); taxpayer portal: 'My Business Account' (Mon dossier d'entreprise). Alberta corporate income tax is administered by CRA under the Federal-Provincial Tax Collection Agreement, so Alberta does not operate a separate corporate income tax filing portal. The Alberta Tax and Revenue Administration (TRA) handles residual provincial fiscal compliance only. Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) administers export declarations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Incorporate under the Alberta Business Corporations Act (ABCA) or under the CBCA with an Alberta extra-provincial registration at the Alberta Corporate Registry. 2) Obtain the 9-digit federal Business Number (BN) via CRA Business Registration Online (BRO) using the Alberta Corporate Access Number; non-resident foreign corporations apply through Form RC4601 with certified charter/registry extracts and a Canadian agent or registered office attestation. 3) Concurrently activate program accounts: RC (federal and Alberta corporate income tax), RT (GST/HST), and RP (payroll) if employees will be resident in Canada. 4) For zero-rated export activities, the RT account is used to file nil/net GST returns and reclaim input tax credits on Canadian production inputs. 5) Online BN issuance is immediate; paper applications take 1-10 business days.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation - A Business Corporation is a separate legal person and statutory taxpayer resident in Canada under Part I of the Income Tax Act (ITA); it is taxed on worldwide income with no flow-through to shareholders. Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) status enables the reduced federal small-business rate (9%) and Alberta's provincial small-business allowance (provincial small-business rate currently 0%); general federal rate 15% plus Alberta general rate 8% apply to non-CCPC income.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no US-style check-the-box regime; ABCA/CBCA incorporation is conclusive for entity classification. Elective mechanisms include ITA s. 85(1) rollover on qualifying incorporation transfers, ITA s. 86(1) share reorganizations, ITA s. 97(2) partnership rollovers, ITA s. 216 net-rental election for non-residents, ITA s. 218.1 dual-resident corporation election, hybrid-mismatch rules under ITA ss. 18.2-18.3 (mandatory, with limited joint designation elections), and ETA s. 150/156 elections for closely related corporations to transact at nil consideration or combine compliance. No election can override the domestic classification of a Canadian corporation; foreign hybrid mismatches involving a US LLC parent are addressed through treaty/domestic-law analysis and advance tax rulings.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Federal Goods and Services Tax (GST) / Harmonized Sales Tax (HST) framework; Alberta applies only the 5% federal GST because the province has no provincial sales tax (PST) and is not an HST participant province.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 gross annual taxable supplies in the preceding four calendar quarters (small-supplier threshold). Once exceeded, GST/HST registration becomes mandatory and tax must be charged; zero-rated exporters of animation and VFX services normally register voluntarily at inception to recover input tax credits on Canadian production inputs.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada has no real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or mandatory validation API comparable to Mexico (CFDI), Italy, or Indonesia. Mandatory electronic filing and electronic remittance apply once annual taxable supplies exceed approximately CAD 1 million. Invoices must meet ETA s. 223 content requirements, and books and records must be retained in readable electronic form under ETA s. 286. The Pan-Canadian e-invoicing framework (voluntary Peppol BIS 3.0) is available but not mandated.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies under ETA Schedule VI Part V s. 7 to services supplied to non-resident persons where the service does not relate to real property situated in Canada or to tangible personal property situated in Canada when performed; commercial 3D animation and CGI character animation delivered digitally to foreign studios qualifies. Part V s. 10 zero-rates supplies of intellectual-property rights to non-residents. The supplier must be a GST/HST registrant, charge 0% output GST, retain evidence of the purchaser's non-resident status, and document that the supply is not for consumption in Canada. No export licence is required for NAICS 512110. Canada imposes no statutory export-FX repatriation deadline; 180 days is used as the internal contractual compliance ceiling.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (B13A/CAED) - mandatory only where physical render media (LTO tapes, portable drives, master discs) are shipped abroad; pure digital deliveries are evidenced by a signed digital-transfer manifest and server/cloud delivery logs

Bill of Lading or Airway Bill - required for physical exports of animation assets; replaced by an electronic handover certificate for encrypted FTP, cloud, or streaming delivery of final animation files

Inward Remittance Certificate (bank MT103/SWIFT credit advice or Wise B2B transaction report) - evidencing receipt of foreign-currency consideration from the non-resident buyer within the 180-day repatriation benchmark
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA's normal GST/HST reassessment window is four years (ETA s. 298); gross negligence extends the window to seven years and fraud carries no limitation period. Late or deficient remittances attract a 5% penalty plus 1% per month with daily prescribed-rate interest (ETA ss. 280-280.1); misrepresentation penalties equal 25% of the tax sought to be evaded (ETA s. 281); false input tax credit claims and unsupported zero-rating are clawed back with statutory interest, retroactively converting zero-rated invoices to 5% taxable supplies. Criminal prosecution under ETA s. 327 and ITA s. 239 exposes directors and officers to fines up to 200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment up to five years. CRA audits zero-rating claims by verifying contemporaneous non-resident status, digital delivery evidence, and bank-level receipt records for each invoice.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); prudential supervision is exercised by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI); currency and AML wire oversight is shared with the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) and the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA). Canada does not maintain a dedicated foreign exchange control commission.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada provides full current-account and capital-account convertibility; there are no exchange controls, currency surrender obligations, or quantitative limits on profit repatriation. Dividends, interest, royalties, and management fees paid to non-residents are subject to Part XIII withholding tax at the statutory 25% rate, reduced by applicable tax treaties. Inbound non-resident equity investment requires nothing more than a permissive Notification under the Investment Canada Act for an entity below the prevailing review thresholds; this SME animation studio is below the monitoring threshold, so no prior review is necessary. The Canadian dollar floats freely and is fully tradable on global FX markets.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory timeline, mandatory conversion ratio, or surrender obligation for export proceeds under Canadian federal or Alberta law. Exporters may maintain foreign-currency accounts offshore or onshore, subject to CRA foreign-asset reporting (Form T1135 for specified foreign property over CAD 100,000; Form T1134/T106 for controlled foreign affiliates or reportable cross-border transactions) and FINTRAC large-value and electronic-funds-transfer reporting thresholds (CAD 10,000). For corporate tax purposes, foreign-currency receipts are translated to CAD at the Bank of Canada daily noon rate or an acceptable forward rate basis under section 261 of the Income Tax Act.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium with conditions. Offshore digital EMI and cross-border payment providers (Wise Business, Airwallex, or similar) may serve as a settlement overlay for CAD, USD, and GBP receipts only if the provider holds a Bank of Canada Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA) registration or operates through a Schedule I Canadian bank sponsor. Unregistered foreign EMIs cannot lawfully provide Canadian-dollar retail payment clearing and create downstream correspondent de-risking exposure. Given the low-risk ISIC 5911 commercial animation profile, a fintech rail is feasible for treasury receivables, but the primary operating and escrow accounts must remain with a federally regulated Canadian chartered bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote eKYC onboarding with liveness verification is normally accepted for a Canadian-resident business corporation in a low-risk commercial sector; however, Tier 1 Canadian banks commonly require an in-person interview at a branch or a registered-agent office when any director or UBO is non-resident, when the entity is newly incorporated without financial statements, or when a foreign parent exercises voting control. For this Alberta corporation, the recommended path is video KYC for resident directors plus a sworn source-of-funds declaration for non-resident shareholders; most Schedule I banks permit full remote opening in this configuration under PCMLTFA reasonable-measures rules.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident UBO or controlling director with no demonstrable Canadian economic substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Alberta Corporate Registry CORES certificate; organizational chart tracing the full indirect ownership chain; notarized passport and residential proof for each director and UBO; bank reference letters from the foreign parent bank; detailed business plan with three-year payment profile; source-of-wealth statement; lease or studio-subbstance documentation evidencing a Canadian operational presence; statutory declaration of tax residence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Recurrent inbound wires from foreign VFX studios, streaming platforms, and ad-tech distributors without visible contractual support
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed work-for-hire agreements; copyright assignment and license contracts; client purchase orders and delivery-acceptance certificates for animation episodes; SWIFT MT103 remittance records showing client identity and invoice references; corporate resolutions authorizing banking signatories; CRA tax-registration confirmations for GST/HST and corporate income tax; FINTRAC-compliant EFT record log; board minute confirming revenues arise solely from NAICS 512110 / ISIC 5911 production services.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large outbound disbursements to non-resident subcontractors or FX-sensitive vendor networks without tax and sanctions documentation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Subcontractor agreements with deliverable milestones and pricing; OFAC and United Nations sanctions screening output for each payee; FINTRAC large-EFT and suspicious-transaction reporting log; Part XIII withholding-tax memorandum with Form NR6 or NR4 certificates; transfer-pricing documentation for non-arm's length service fees; SWIFT MT103 instruction history with valid purpose codes; board-approved monthly treasury and payment registry.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant route: non-resident shareholder equity or intercompany loan remitted via SWIFT MT103; Field 70 must carry an ISO 20022 purpose code such as CAPC (capital contribution) or FINV (foreign direct investment), and the MT103 must identify the recipient Canadian financial institution, transit number, and account number. Equity injections must be recorded through corporate resolution and share-certificate issuance in the minute book; shareholder loans require a promissory note priced at the CRA prescribed annual rate to avoid a benefits/ADA tax issue. The receiving bank verifies the recipient's CRA corporate tax account (RT) and GST/HST account before first deposit. The Investment Canada Act review threshold is not exceeded for this entity; a post-closing notification is sufficient if any filing is made at all. Funds clear on bank business days via LVTS or correspondent USD clearing networks.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Domestic CAD operating settlements use LVTS real-time wires or EFT bulk debit/credit rails; cross-border commercial settlements use SWIFT MT103 member-to-member correspondent clearing with verified Standard Settlement Instructions; USD settlements clear through Fedwire or CHIPS via the Canadian bank's New York correspondent. For high-value distribution milestones, an irrevocable documentary letter of credit confirmed by a Canadian Schedule I bank may be issued under UCP600, although this is not market standard for 3D animation work-for-hire. A standby letter of credit or performance bond may be used only where a counterparty conditions payments on performance security. Payments to non-resident service vendors must evidence Part XIII withholding calculations and Form NR6/NR4 compliance before wire execution.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign exchange forwards with a Canadian Schedule I bank under an IFX/ISDA-style master agreement
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for emerging-market currency exposures documented under the ISDA 2002 Master Agreement
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) with ISDA 2002/1992 and CSA collateral documentation
FX options and zero-cost option collars with a regulated Schedule I bank for corporate hedging purposes
Short-term FX swaps for treasury cash conversion with a regulated Canadian chartered bank

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing must be completed within one (1) month after the corporation's incorporation anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing incurs a CAD 50 penalty; failure to file for three (3) consecutive years authorizes the Registrar to administratively dissolve (strike-off) the corporation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal T2 Corporation Income Tax Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Six (6) months after the corporation's fiscal year end; filing 10-year carryback may apply
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty is 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month, to 12%; repeated failures add 10% penalty plus compliance requirements; director liability may attach for unpaid withholdings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Six (6) months after the corporation's fiscal year end, consistent with the federal T2 deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of balance due, plus 1% per full month (maximum 12 months), and interest compounded daily on unpaid Alberta corporate tax.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Alberta Business Corporations Act, an independent audit is mandatory where shareholders holding more than 5% of the issued shares resolve to require an audit, or pursuant to a unanimous shareholder agreement. Financial institutions, securities issuers, and specified regulated entities are separately audited. Private corporations below the Canada Revenue Agency gross-revenue threshold (for associated corporations) are not required to file audited financial statements but must maintain adequate records.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS is mandatory for public corporations and certain regulated entities; private corporations may apply ASPE (Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises). All financial records must be prepared in accordance with accepted accounting standards appropriate for the entity type.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Canada Business Corporations Act and applicable provincial law, the corporation must maintain a register of individuals with significant control (ISC), reporting any ownership, control, or direction of 25% or more of shares within 15 days of change. Annual confirmation is required during the annual return process, including disclosure of controlled entity ownership and ISC registers for the preceding year.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC Register)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 23.0% combined federal and Alberta general corporate income tax rate (Federal 15% after abatement and general rate reduction + Alberta 8%). A Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) pays a combined 11.0% on the first CA$500,000 of active business income (Federal 9% + Alberta 2%). The general rate applies to passive and foreign-controlled corporate income.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SR&ED refundable investment tax credit: 35% (CCPC) or 15% (non-CCPC) of qualifying R&D expenditures, highly relevant for proprietary rendering software. CAVCO Canadian Film or Video Production Tax Credit: 25% of certified Canadian labour expenditure (T2 line 610). Film or Video Production Services Tax Credit: 16% of Canadian labour costs for foreign-owned productions (T2 line 611). Alberta Film and Television Tax Credit: refundable credit, category-dependent up to 30% of eligible Alberta labour expenditure with regional uplift; refundable credits can exceed tax payable and produce a net cash refund. Alberta imposes no provincial capital tax.
